newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan c/a surplus seen on downtrend for now - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan c/a surplus seen on downtrend for now - MOF.

text.p: Japan's current account surplus is seen continuing to stay on a downtrend, a Ministry of Finance (MOF) official told a press briefing on Monday.

The volume of imports has continued to grow at a much faster pace than that of exports, while a deficit in the service account, especially a deficit in the travel account, has been expanding robustly, the official said.
"We believe the current shrinking trend in the current account surplus would continue for now," he said.
Earlier, the ministry said Japan's current account surplus shrank 27.3 percent to 568.2 billion yen in July from a year earlier. The surplus has been falling since September 1995.

The surplus in merchandise trade alone also fell to 730.1 billion yen, down 26.4 percent from the same month a year ago, marking the 20th straight month of year-on-year declines. The July trade surplus was the smallest for any July since the ministry began tracking comparable data in January 1985.
The ministry official said car exports appeared to have hit a major bottom after earlier declines resulting from Japanese manufacturers' active shift of production abroad.
"With the volume of exports growing again in July, the manufacturers' trend of shifting their production overseas appears to be taking a breather now," the official said.
